rationale: Tests understanding of the sequential steps of bilirubin metabolism from haem degradation to faecal excretion, the biochemical basis for interpreting bilirubin fractions in LFT reports.
Tests the ability to match each adrenal cortex zone to its principal hormone product, building the spatial map needed for interpreting cortisol, aldosterone and androgen levels in adrenal disease.
Tests the ability to classify liver function test results into hepatocellular, cholestatic and haemolytic patterns, the central skill for interpreting LFT reports in clinical practice.
Tests recall of the key values and terms for classifying azotaemia and proteinuria, which distinguish pre-renal from intrinsic renal causes at the bedside.
Tests recall of the key values and terms used in early pregnancy monitoring and prenatal screening, which underpin the clinical decisions around ectopic pregnancy and trisomy risk.
Tests recall of the key components of the cytochrome P450 monooxygenase reaction, which underpins all Phase I drug metabolism and enzyme-induction interactions.
Tests the ability to match each major Phase II conjugation reaction to its clinical context, reinforcing how conjugation pathways determine drug clearance, neonatal jaundice and toxicity.

Tests understanding of the step-by-step mechanism of paracetamol hepatotoxicity from normal metabolism through glutathione depletion to centrilobular necrosis, which underpins the rationale for early NAC treatment.

Tests the ability to order the enzymatic antioxidant relay from superoxide generation through SOD and glutathione peroxidase to NADPH-dependent glutathione regeneration, the pathway that links G6PD deficiency to oxidant drug sensitivity.

Tests the ability to identify the four downstream pathways in Brownlee's unifying mechanism of hyperglycaemic damage, which explains why a single metabolic excess causes multiple diabetic complications.
